# Plan an aquatic-animal video study

Start with your scientific question, not the number of cameras. AquaTrajectories accepts 2D and 3D timestamped observations, but camera geometry and independent reference data determine which claims can be defended.

<nav class="aqt-path-chooser" aria-label="Select a recording configuration">
<a href="#one-camera">One camera · 2D</a>
<a href="#two-cameras">Two cameras · conditional 3D</a>
<a href="#existing-recordings">I already have video</a>

## One camera

**Typical purpose:** planar locations, camera-local trajectories, visible group geometry and carefully defined 2D zones. Record original video, codec details, frame IDs and presentation timestamps. If converting pixels to physical units, independently establish a suitable spatial scale and confirm the assumptions of the measurement plane. A single conventional camera does not recover unconstrained underwater depth.

For detection accuracy, independently review fish bounding boxes **and empty frames**; unresolved biological identities should stay unresolved. Camera-local track numbers are not automatically stable biological fish identities.

**Relevant methods:** `aqt_import_mot()`, `aqt_import_yolo()`, `aqt_track_qc()`, `aqt_kinematics()`, `aqt_group_metrics()`. See [video tracking](video-tracking.html) and [movement and schooling](movement-and-schooling.html).

## Two cameras

**Typical purpose:** multiview observations that may support 3D reconstruction after suitable calibration and association. Two GoPros alone do **not** guarantee physical XYZ accuracy.

Record both source videos and original time bases. Plan independently identified shared timing markers or external hardware exposure evidence; estimate clock offset/drift against holdout markers. Document camera intrinsics and pose, lens distortion, tank walls, refractive interfaces and calibration settings. Establish cross-camera fish correspondence, including abstention when ambiguous.

A physical XYZ-accuracy claim further requires **separately surveyed underwater targets**, withheld from fitting and distributed over depths and tank regions. Report invalid reconstructions as well as valid-point error.

**Relevant methods:** `aqt_sync_holdout_fit()`, `aqt_refractive_triangulate()`, `aqt_target_holdout_benchmark()`. Closest-ray distance and reprojection residuals are internal consistency, not independently surveyed truth. See [multiview 3D](multiview-3d.html).

## Existing recordings

Preserve the originals and complete a preflight audit before generating movement statistics:

1. Register each recording/session/camera and source SHA-256 digest; retain original frame indices and presentation timestamps.
2. Document the external detector checkpoint, thresholds, preprocessing, tracker and any overlap with evaluation video.
3. Check annotation provenance, reviewed empty frames, gaps and unknown fish IDs.
4. Locate actual calibration, exposure timing and independently measured physical targets; never substitute model output for those records.
5. Restrict 3D, identity and welfare claims when those reference data are absent.

See [video to results](video-to-results.html), the [validation matrix](capabilities-and-validation.html), and [evidence dashboard](research-evidence-dashboard.html).

## Before recording

- [ ] Define the estimand (detection, individual movement, 3D XYZ, group structure or intervention contrast).
- [ ] Record fish species, density, tank dimensions, lighting, camera placement and occlusion conditions.
- [ ] Preserve original videos, frame manifests, timestamps, device settings, hashes and detector/version identifiers.
- [ ] Plan a prediction-blind annotation sample, including reviewed empty frames and unresolved identities.
- [ ] For multiple cameras, record independent sync markers, geometry and withheld submerged XYZ reference targets.
- [ ] For intervention studies, allocate and document **independent tanks**; frames are repeated measurements, not treatment replicates.
- [ ] Record event timings on a documented clock; retain ethics and permission records.

The [experiment starter kit](experiment-starter-kit.html) provides synthetic examples, event logs and **blank** physical reference-target templates. These are not real fish observations. The [interactive teaching lab](../synthetic-explorer.html) demonstrates camera viewpoints and identity errors with invented data.
